# Tasks Document

> Sequencing: Track A (typecheck) lands first and brings the shared infra (`path-denylist`, `adversarial-settings` module, `Promise.allSettled` shell, `validateAllFiles`, hygiene denylist filter, methodology composite-pin scaffold). Track B (diff) slots into the existing seam and replaces the Track-A interim fixtures. Track C (per-runner model selection) touches the `multi-server.ts` route handlers and adds annotation persistence. Composite-pin tests are the safety net per R4.10.

## Track A — Typecheck pre-computation + shared infra

- [ ] 1. Create path-denylist module in src/core/path-denylist.ts
  - File: src/core/path-denylist.ts
  - Implement `partitionPaths(paths)` returning `{ kept, skipped }` and export `TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS`.
  - Implement match semantics from R1.5 / design §`path-denylist.ts`: exact basenames, basename suffixes, basename prefixes, path-segment match. NOT shell globs / git pathspec wildcards.
  - Cross-platform segment splitting on both `/` and `\` regardless of host platform; strip Windows drive-letter prefix before segmentation; filter empty-string segments (UNC, doubled separators); reject empty denylist entries at construction time.
  - Case-folding rules: secret-bearing basenames/suffixes/prefixes always case-folded; lock-file basenames + binary-suffix entries case-folded only on case-insensitive volumes; path-segment matches unconditionally case-insensitive.
  - Test-fixture exception (R1.6 narrowed) applies ONLY to path-segment denylist; basename/suffix/prefix rules continue to apply to fixture paths.
  - Purpose: single source of truth for lock/secret/binary path filtering, consumed by both `computeTaskDiff` (Track B) and `computeHygieneSignals`.
  - _Leverage: node:path only (no other dependencies)_
  - _Requirements: 1.5, 1.6_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer specializing in cross-platform path handling and security-adjacent allow/denylist logic | Task: Create `src/core/path-denylist.ts` per design §`src/core/path-denylist.ts` and requirements R1.5/R1.6, exporting `partitionPaths(paths)` and `TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS`; implement exact-basename + suffix + prefix + path-segment matching with the exact case-folding rules listed in the design; split segments on both `/` and `\`, strip Windows drive-letter prefixes, filter empty segments, reject empty entries at construction | Restrictions: Do NOT use shell globs or git pathspec wildcards; do NOT add runtime dependencies beyond `node:path`; do NOT widen the test-fixture exception beyond path-segment matches (basename/suffix/prefix rules still apply to fixture paths); keep `partitionPaths` pure and synchronous | _Leverage: node:path | _Requirements: R1.5, R1.6 | Success: `partitionPaths` correctly classifies the cases listed in design §Testing/`path-denylist.test.ts` (mixed-separator inputs Linux+`secrets\foo.json` and Windows+`secrets/foo.json`, secret-bearing case-fold, lock-file conditional case-fold, path-segment unconditional case-insensitive, fixture exception). After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when the implementation is done, then mark the task complete._

- [ ] 2. Add path-denylist tests in src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts
  - File: src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts
  - Cover per-category case-folding, narrowed test-fixture exception, mixed-separator inputs (Linux + `secrets\foo.json` skips; Windows + `secrets/foo.json` skips), Windows drive-letter stripping, empty-segment filtering, empty-entry rejection at construction.
  - Purpose: pin denylist behavior so future entries don't silently regress cross-platform agent → reviewer flows.
  - _Leverage: vitest, src/core/path-denylist.ts_
  - _Requirements: 1.5, 1.6_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in vitest and cross-platform path semantics | Task: Write `src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts` covering the cases listed in design §Testing for `path-denylist.test.ts` per R1.5/R1.6 | Restrictions: Do NOT mock `node:path`; tests must be deterministic on both POSIX and Windows; do NOT collapse "case-folded only on case-insensitive volumes" into a platform-blind assertion | _Leverage: vitest, src/core/path-denylist.ts | _Requirements: R1.5, R1.6 | Success: All listed cases pass; mixed-separator bypass cases fail without the cross-platform splitting code (verified by mutation). After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

- [ ] 3. Create adversarial-settings module in src/core/adversarial-settings.ts
  - File: src/core/adversarial-settings.ts
  - Export `RunnerKey`, `AdversarialSettings`, `loadSettings(projectPath)`, `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)`, `isTypecheckEnabled(settings)`.
  - `loadSettings`: in-process cache keyed by `(absPath, mtime, size)`; wrap `statSync`/`readFileSync` in try/catch covering `EBUSY`/`EACCES`/`EISDIR`/`ELOOP`/`ENOENT`/other (ENOENT silent → `{}`; all others `{}` + warn-once); JSON.parse failures → `{}` + warn-once; pinned warning format `[spec-workflow] adversarial-settings.json: <reason> (path: <absPath>); falling back to defaults. <one-line parser/IO error message>`; warn-once flag per absPath, cleared when `(mtime, size)` advances. NO I/O throw escapes.
  - `resolveRunnerModel`: grouped non-empty string > legacy non-empty string > `undefined`; non-string `model` warn-once and fall through; empty string treated as "explicitly cleared"; `null` runner block treated as absent.
  - `isTypecheckEnabled`: `false` only when `features.typecheck === false`; non-boolean values warn-once and default to `true`; `features` non-object treated as absent + warn-once.
  - Purpose: central settings reader with bounded I/O, used by Track A (typecheck enable) and Track C (model resolution).
  - _Leverage: node:fs, node:path, src/core/path-utils.ts (PathUtils.getWorkflowRoot)_
  - _Requirements: 3.1–3.7, 3.10, 3.12_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer specializing in defensive I/O and config-precedence logic | Task: Create `src/core/adversarial-settings.ts` per design §`src/core/adversarial-settings.ts` and requirements R3.1–R3.7, R3.10, R3.12; implement `loadSettings`, `resolveRunnerModel`, `isTypecheckEnabled` with the exact precedence ladder, edge cases, and warn-once semantics described | Restrictions: NO I/O throw may escape `loadSettings`; warn-once is per-absPath and per-cause-class; do NOT cache across `(mtime, size)` changes; do NOT add async surface — `loadSettings` is sync per design (handlePrepare's prelude is sync); do NOT pass non-string model values through to `runner.run` | _Leverage: node:fs sync APIs, src/core/path-utils.ts | _Requirements: R3.1–R3.7, R3.10, R3.12 | Success: All edge cases in R3.5 (empty string, null, non-object, non-string, unknown sub-keys) handled per spec; warn-once format matches pinned string; cache hit avoids re-parse. After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

  - Cover R3.10 precedence matrix (a–g cases from design + R3.10 list), cache hit/miss with `utimes()` mid-session edit, read-throw containment (`EBUSY`/`EACCES`/`EISDIR`/`ELOOP` simulated via `vi.spyOn(fs, 'readFileSync')`), `isTypecheckEnabled` non-boolean warn, `resolveRunnerModel` non-string `model` warn, cold-cache integration test (timed first call, regression bound).
  - Purpose: pin settings reader behavior including failure modes.
  - _Leverage: vitest, src/core/adversarial-settings.ts, node:fs/promises (utimes for cache invalidation tests)_
  - _Requirements: 3.1–3.7, 3.10, 3.12_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: QA Engineer with expertise in vitest mocking and filesystem cache invalidation testing | Task: Write `src/core/__tests__/adversarial-settings.test.ts` covering the cases in design §Testing for `adversarial-settings.test.ts` and R3.10 | Restrictions: Use `vi.spyOn(fs, 'readFileSync')` to inject I/O errors; use `fs.promises.utimes` to advance mtime for cache invalidation; do NOT skip the warn-once dedup test (must verify second identical-cause read is silent until mtime/size advances) | _Leverage: vitest, node:fs/promises | _Requirements: R3.1–R3.7, R3.10, R3.12 | Success: All seven precedence cases (a–g) pass; cache evict/refresh on `(mtime, size)` change verified; warn-once pinned format asserted exactly; ENOENT silent, others warned. After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

- [ ] 5. Create typecheck utility in src/core/typecheck.ts
  - File: src/core/typecheck.ts
  - Export `TypecheckDiagnostic`, `TypecheckResult` (discriminated union), and `runProjectTypecheck(projectPath, allFiles, opts)`.
  - Behavior per design §`src/core/typecheck.ts`: feature-disabled short-circuit; tsconfig resolution (`no-tsconfig` / `project-references` / `wrapper-config`); resolve `tsc` from `node_modules/.bin/tsc` (`tsc-not-found`); `mkdir .spec-workflow/.cache` (recursive) before spawning; spawn `tsc --noEmit -p . --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile <projectPath>/.spec-workflow/.cache/tsc.tsbuildinfo --listFiles --pretty false` with `env: { ...process.env, FORCE_COLOR: '0', NO_COLOR: '1' }`, `maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`, 30s timeout (SIGTERM → 2s grace → SIGKILL, POSIX-primary).
  - Two-pass parse: Pass 1 walks lines for diagnostics with multi-line continuation (subsequent indented lines that don't match an absolute-path shape AND don't match TS/JS source-file shape `/\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mts|cts|mjs|cjs)(:|$)/` are appended to current diagnostic's `message`); per-diagnostic message size cap 4 KB with `\n<...truncated>` suffix; TS2418/TS2417 related-info siblings are sibling diagnostics (not absorbed). Pass 2: from unconsumed lines, keep only absolute-path-shaped lines for `--listFiles`.
  - Async path normalization: `fs.promises.realpath` chunks of 100, per-path try/catch for ENOENT (bucket as `coverage.excluded` using original path), case-fold to lowercase on case-insensitive volumes; reported arrays use original `allFiles` paths deduped by normalized form.
  - Tag each diagnostic with `inScope`. Apply `partitionPaths` to `coverage.compiled`, `coverage.excluded`, `diagnostics[].file`; surface dropped count as `suppressedDenylistedFiles`. Cap diagnostics at 100 (in-scope first), set `truncated: true` when capped.
  - Surface `typecheckWarning: 'tsbuildinfo rebuild — concurrent prepare suspected'` on detected buildinfo-rebuild stderr signature.
  - Purpose: pre-compute tsc diagnostics + coverage so reviewer triages instead of hunts.
  - _Leverage: node:child_process (execFile), node:fs/promises, node:path, src/core/path-denylist.ts_
  - _Requirements: 2.1–2.14_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in child_process orchestration, tsc output parsing, and process-termination semantics | Task: Implement `src/core/typecheck.ts` per design §`src/core/typecheck.ts` and R2.1–R2.14, returning the discriminated `TypecheckResult` union; never throw to caller; convert all expected failures to `unavailable` reasons or `timeout` | Restrictions: Do NOT import `typescript` as a library — invoke the project's own `node_modules/.bin/tsc`; do NOT skip the multi-line continuation parse (TS2345/TS2322 type-expansion lines must be captured); do NOT absorb TS2418/TS2417 related-info as continuation (they are sibling diagnostics); do NOT cap message size before applying continuation join; ENOENT realpath errors bucket as `excluded`, all other realpath errors propagate via warn-once; do NOT silently degrade clean-exit + empty `--listFiles` to `success` with empty compiled set — surface `'no-parseable-output'`; honor `opts.enabled === false` short-circuit before any I/O | _Leverage: node:child_process execFile, node:fs/promises, node:path, src/core/path-denylist.ts | _Requirements: R2.1–R2.14 | Success: All `unavailable` reasons reachable; in-scope tagging works against pnpm-symlinked workspace paths; 100-cap with in-scope-first ordering verified; multi-line TS2345 expansion captured. After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

- [ ] 8. Add validateAllFiles helper + Promise.allSettled shell to handlePrepare in src/tools/review-task.ts
  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify, after `allFiles` is computed at ~line 180)
  - Add module-private `validateAllFiles(input, projectPath)` per design §`validateAllFiles` — per-element try/catch around `path.resolve` and `safeRealpath`; symlink-target inside-projectPath check using realpath'd both sides; asymmetric undefined handling (projectPath undefined → fall back to literal; entry undefined → drop with warn-once).

In Track A's PR, `computeTaskDiff` is replaced by a stub that resolves to `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths: [], truncated: false }` — the seam is in place; Track B fills the diff utility in. (Note: hygiene was already wired; preserve its behavior.)

  - Add the new `data` fields: `diff`, `diffStats`, `skippedPaths`, `diffTruncated`, `diffRejection` (placeholder values until Track B), `typecheckResults`, `hygieneRejection`. Keep `filesToReview`, `hygieneSignals`, `methodology`, `taskContext`, `implementationSummary`, `steeringExcerpt` shape unchanged.
  - Purpose: orchestration shell that the three utilities slot into; Track B is purely additive at this seam.
  - _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts, src/core/adversarial-settings.ts, src/core/hygiene-signals.ts, src/core/path-utils.ts (warnOnce conventions)_
  - _Requirements: 2.12, 1.4 (degraded-state contract), all R4 directive surface fields_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer maintaining `src/tools/review-task.ts` `handlePrepare` | Task: Add `validateAllFiles`, `safeRealpath`, the `Promise.allSettled` shell, and the three `unwrap*` helpers per design §`handlePrepare`; wire `loadSettings`/`isTypecheckEnabled` into the prelude; add the new `data` fields with placeholder diff values (Track B fills in `computeTaskDiff`) | Restrictions: Per-element try/catch in `validateAllFiles` MUST cover NUL-byte, Symbol/BigInt-coerced, non-string, and `path.resolve` throws; `safeRealpath` MUST catch all realpath I/O errors (ENOENT silent, others warn-once); the inside-projectPath check MUST realpath BOTH sides; `safeRealpath(entry)` undefined MUST drop the entry (do NOT fall back to original-path prefix comparison); `unwrap*` warn-once key MUST be `(utility, error.message)` not just `(utility)`; do NOT remove or reshape existing data fields | _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts, src/core/adversarial-settings.ts, src/core/hygiene-signals.ts, warnOnce | _Requirements: R2.12 + degraded-state contracts | Success: handlePrepare resolves under all three-utility-rejection scenarios with structurally-distinguishable degraded states; `validateAllFiles` boundary tests all pass; settings load failure does not propagate. After completing, set the task to in-progress in tasks.md, run log-implementation when done, then mark the task complete._

  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify `buildReviewMethodology`)
  - Add new arguments per design §`buildReviewMethodology`: `diffState: DiffMethodologyState`, `typecheckState: TypecheckMethodologyState`. ## Track B — Diff-first context

- [ ] 12. Create task-diff utility in src/core/task-diff.ts
